claim: For every integer \(q\ge1\) and all \(m,n\ge3\), the directed successor cycles \(D_m,D_n\) are indistinguishable by first-order sentences of quantifier rank at most \(q\) exactly when the corresponding undirected cycles \(C_m,C_n\) are; equivalently, the size cutoff is \(3\) at rank one, \(4\) at rank two, and \(2^{q-1}+3\) for every \(q\ge3\).

correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge3\), undirected adjacency is quantifier-free definable as S(x,y) or S(y,x), so the published lower bound transfers at unchanged rank. Rank one and rank two are checked directly. For \(q\ge3\), the published cycle-cut gap strategy has an order-preserving form; matching short gaps exactly and keeping long gaps above the stage threshold preserves the directed successor relation. The resulting cutoff is exactly \(2^{q-1}+3\).
